prompt:
can you turn our release notes process into a skill? every friday someone runs `git log --merges v<last>..HEAD`, groups the PRs by label (feat / fix / chore, chore gets left out), and writes notes in CHANGELOG.md under a new `## vX.Y.Z (date)` heading. it has to be user-facing language, not PR titles. breaking changes go first under a **Breaking** line, and anything touching api/public/ needs a line in docs/migration.md too.

gotcha that bites every new person: PRs merged by the merge bot have the label on the linked issue, not on the PR. you get it with `gh pr view N --json closingIssuesReferences`. and the version number comes from `scripts/next-version.sh`, don't guess it.

people on the team use both claude code and codex so it needs to work in both. put it in a folder called release-notes/
assertions: release-notes/SKILL.md exists and starts with YAML frontmatter that has `name` and `description`
The frontmatter of release-notes/SKILL.md uses only these fields: name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools
The description says what the skill does and when to use it, and is under 1,024 characters
The description does not tell the agent to use the skill for any mention of git, commits, changelogs or versions in general
The body says that PRs merged by the merge bot carry the label on the linked issue and gives `gh pr view N --json closingIssuesReferences`
The body says to get the version from `scripts/next-version.sh`
The body says that a change touching api/public/ needs a line in docs/migration.md
The body has no section whose heading is about when to use the skill
release-notes/SKILL.md contains none of these words in capitals: CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS
The release-notes/ folder contains no README, changelog or installation guide of its own
The body gives the heading format `## vX.Y.Z (date)` and says breaking changes go first under a Breaking line
